# jaspatial
<!-- badges: start -->
```{r, out.width = "200px", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("jaspatial_logo.png")
```

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of jaspatial is to set up your environment to conduct geospatial analyses at January Advisors and provide 
a repository of common functions we have developed. 

## Installation

And the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("januaryadvisors/jaspatial")
```
## Set up your environment

When you start a geospatial analysis, load the `jaspatial` library and then load all the other common geospatial packages and set the correct options:

```{r example}
library(jaspatial)
load_geo_packages() 
#This will load: sf, tigris, tidycensus, mapview, 
  #leaflet, leaflet.extras, leaflet.extras2, rmapshaper,
set_geo_options() #Set the correct options for tigris downloads
```

## Clean your data
You can also quickly clean and transform the projection of an sf object using `clean_shape`. The default projection that comes pre-loaded is `wgs84`. But you can use others, too.

```{r clean_shape}
clean_tx_counties <- clean_shape(tx_counties) #The default 

#Or change projection
utm14n <- st_crs("+proj=utm +zone=14 +ellps=GRS80 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs +towgs84=0,0,0")
clean_tx_counties_utm14n <- clean_shape(tx_counties, utm14n)
```

## Set your CARTO basemap key (do this once)

CARTO watermarks basemap tiles requested without an API key, so every map renders
with "API KEY REQUIRED" stamped across it. Set the key once and every JA project on
your machine picks it up:

``` r
usethis::edit_r_environ()   # add the line below, then restart R
# CARTO_API_KEY=your_key_here
```

Get a key at <https://carto.com/basemaps/apikey/>. Check that it resolved with
`ja_carto_key()`.

`jaspatial` looks in four places, first non-empty wins:

1. `options(jaspatial.carto_key = "...")`, a session override
2. `CARTO_API_KEY` in a project `.env` (needs the `dotenv` package)
3. `Sys.getenv("CARTO_API_KEY")`, which covers `~/.Renviron` and CI
4. a `carto: CARTO_API_KEY` entry in `config.yml` (needs the `config` package)

A project `.env` beats `~/.Renviron` on purpose, so a project can pin its own key.

Without a key nothing breaks: you get one warning and a watermarked map.

**Working locally with a domain-restricted key.** A key limited to your published
domains leaves maps blank in the RStudio viewer and local Shiny, because CARTO
refuses it off those domains. Create a second CARTO key that lists only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and
`*.localhost`, and add it next to the first in `~/.Renviron`:

``` r
# CARTO_API_KEY_LOCAL=your_local_key
```

Maps then switch to it automatically when served from `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`
(the RStudio viewer, local Shiny, a local preview server) and keep the production
key everywhere else, including pages you render locally and publish. An HTML file
opened straight from disk shows no basemap with either key, so preview it through
a local server such as `servr::httd()`.

**Deploying to shinyapps.io** does not carry your `.env`, so pass the key through:

``` r
rsconnect::deployApp(envVars = "CARTO_API_KEY")
```

The key is used client-side and is visible in any rendered HTML. That is how
browser basemaps work. Keeping it out of the source tree is about rotation, not
secrecy. Restrict it by domain in the CARTO dashboard, remembering that dashboards
iframed on client sites need those domains allowed too.

## Check what you published

Rendered pages regress quietly: nothing errors, the tiles just come back stamped.
After a render, and before publishing:

``` r
ja_audit_basemaps("docs")
#> Scanned 106 files under docs; 89 draw a basemap.
#> All basemaps are keyed.
```

## Using leaflet
This package allows you to get up and running in leaflet really quickly with `ja_base_map`. The one trick is that you need to add a mapPane option (='polygons') to any layers you want to appear underneath the map label names.

Building your own `leaflet()` instead? Use `add_carto_basemap()` as a drop-in for
`addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron")`, and `add_carto_labels()` for the labels
overlay. `addProviderTiles()` cannot carry a key, because the CartoDB entry in the
leaflet-providers registry has no placeholder for one.

``` r
leaflet() %>%
  add_carto_basemap() %>%
  addPolygons(data = clean_tx_counties)
```

```{r ja_base_map, warning=FALSE}
ja_base_map(.zoom_level = 9) %>% 
  addPolygons(
    data = clean_tx_counties,
    options = leafletOptions(pane = "polygons")
  )
```
